scope: Cumulative v0.1.0-alpha.3 -> v0.1.0-alpha.4 release-candidate AOT performance: whole-process callgrind instruction counts (Ir) of the 23 adapted pyperformance benchmarks plus bench/fib.py, bench/nbody.py, bench/spectral.py and a reduced-size microGPT. Each candidate source is built by both compilers, so differences come from compiler, library and runtime. Instruction counts, not wall-time claims.

revisions.inputs: benchmark sources from the candidate checkout; every bench/pyperformance/*.py, bench/fib.py, bench/nbody.py, bench/spectral.py and bench/microgpt/microgpt.py blob equals c3aaa068's

toolchain.host: shared 4-vCPU Linux x86-64 VM (Firecracker), Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz; three other agents active

environment.variables: Every build and run gets an explicit minimal environment: PATH, HOME, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8. No inherited PYSTACHY_*, PYTHONPATH, PYTHONHOME or PYTHONUNBUFFERED.
environment.builds: pystachy build SOURCE -o EXE, run from the compiler's own checkout directory with PYSTACHY_HOME set to that checkout and a private PYSTACHY_CACHE per compiler ($SCRATCH/perf/cache-alpha3, $SCRATCH/perf/cache-candidate), each warmed by building a hello-world program first (cold-cache builds: alpha.3 5.10 s, candidate 7.15 s). Builds took the shared $SCRATCH/build.lock (flock) so they did not overlap other agents' builds.
environment.runs: Executables and CPython run from an empty directory ($SCRATCH/perf/run); microgpt from $SCRATCH/perf/inputs/microgpt-run, which holds input.txt. Every build, CPython run, callgrind run and wall sample is pinned with taskset -c 3.

method.instruction_counts: valgrind --tool=callgrind --error-exitcode=99 --callgrind-out-file=FILE EXE ARGS; the whole-process 'summary:' Ir. One run per executable: for a fixed binary, arguments and environment, counts repeat to within a few tens of instructions (see reproducibility).
method.oracle: python3.13 -s -P SOURCE ARGS (CPython 3.13.18) with the same environment and arguments; each executable's stdout under callgrind is compared byte for byte with the oracle's stdout.
method.arguments: The controller's measured arguments (tools/bench_pyperformance.py BENCHMARKS[name][0]) where they give roughly 0.3-2 billion instructions; otherwise the loop count is scaled (per-benchmark 'controller_measured_args' shows the original). The same arguments are used for both compilers and CPython.
method.build_time_and_size: Single build per compiler and benchmark on a warmed runtime cache: wall seconds and executable bytes are indicative only (shared host). The candidate's AOT pipeline adds #1020's late step (clang -O2 -emit-llvm, opt forceattrs/always-inline of pys_new, then clang -O2 -c -Xclang -disable-llvm-passes) to alpha.3's single clang -O2 -c.
method.attribution: callgrind_annotate --inclusive=no --threshold=100 --auto=no on both profiles; object paths dropped so functions compare by name. callgrind's 'NAME'2' entries are recursion levels (--separate-recs default). Call counts from the profiles' calls= records; recursion-depth accesses confirmed in objdump -d of the measured executables.

reproducibility.retained_json_control: json_loads 300 executables are byte-identical to the retained broad JSON control's (bench/smoke/results/json-controls-2026-11-02.json: alpha.3 61a3a680daf89e122b404dc6f73f33fd64afb7a6665fbff90a0edd43edfa878f, candidate 4f086575f1a27af6bb7138667ec0c78530561479cca8bc89220ae9ce88f4adc8), so both compilers, libraries and runtimes reproduce that record's builds. Counts here: 1,300,276,404 and 1,428,396,351 (+9.853%); retained: 1,300,394,281 and 1,428,523,891 (+9.853%). The 0.009% offset on both sides is environmental: with this run's minimal environment glibc's __tunables_init scans fewer variables (-105,777 Ir) and GC/stack work changes slightly.
reproducibility.repeat_runs: Repeating two counts with the same executable, arguments and environment gave scimark 8 (candidate) 735,780,715 versus 735,780,736 and fannkuch 1 (alpha.3) 868,840,650 versus 868,840,644; the experiment's scimark repeat differed by 19. Each program prints its varying timed seconds and reads the clock, so counts repeat to within a few tens of instructions (about 3e-8), far below every reported change.
reproducibility.inputs: Benchmark source SHA-256s are per benchmark (input_sha256); compiler binary SHA-256s under 'compilers'.

attribution.selection: The three largest instruction regressions above +2%: bench_fib (+24.13%), scimark (+22.09%) and generators (+13.32%). json_loads (+9.85%) is the known #1004 byte-scanner result and is only confirmed here. Function-level notes for the other regressions above +2% follow.

top3.evidence: All +104,512,679 Ir is in fib itself (f.fib -> closed-recursion body r.f.fib): 29,860,703 calls, +3.500 instructions per call. objdump of the candidate's r.f.fib shows the depth argument compared with pys_recursion_state+8 (the limit), incremented and kept across the first recursive call; alpha.3's f.fib has no recursion state. docs/reports/recursion-guard-policy.md records the same AOT cost (fib 433.3M on pre-#996 main, +24.12%; 'its closed form adds 3.5 per call'), an accepted cost of catchable RecursionError.

top3.cause: #888 (6daa6aea, numeric list item identity): the identity-companion line in runtime.c pys_list_set, inlined into every typed list store
top3.evidence: +130,827,200 of +133,115,220 Ir is in f.FFT_transform_internal.1 (+38.8%), plus +4.8M in Random.nextDouble. Both compilers emit the same FFT IR up to block order and value numbering (identical sorted instruction multiset; 8 pys_list_set and 12 pys_list_get calls), but the linked -O2 function is 546 instructions instead of 317. pys_list_set gained 'if (l->ids) { l->ids[i + 1] = 0; if (!big_list(l)) l->ids[0] |= 4; }' in #888; #979's pys_plain opt_in() trap does not cover this store, so plain programs keep it. Experiment: the candidate compiler with a scratch copy of c3aaa068 whose runtime.c omits only that line rebuilds FFT_transform_internal at exactly 317 instructions, and scimark 8 counts 573,678,724 Ir (a repeat: 573,678,743; 4.81% below alpha.3, 22.03% below the candidate) with stdout matching CPython; FFT_transform_internal and Random.nextDouble return to alpha.3's exact self costs.

top3.cause: #996 (eac64613): counted resumes of the recursive Tree.__iter__ generator
top3.evidence: Tree.__iter__'s recursive resumes (17,258,423, identical in both) cost +113,108,839 Ir (+6.55 per resume); top-level resumes +7.0 each; the new pys.gen.drop.counted runs 1,100,008 times (+17,600,128, 16 per drop); f.tree became closed recursion (+1.9M). GC work shifts (scan -22.7M, collect +17.3M). objdump: the candidate's m.Tree.__iter__.resume accesses pys_recursion_state 15 times and calls pys_recursion_error twice; alpha.3's has neither. docs/reports/recursion-guard-policy.md reports generators AOT +10.93% for #996 against its own baseline ('about 17 counted generator resumes per value, which keep the depth word').

known.note: Confirms the retained broad JSON control: byte-identical executables (alpha.3 61a3a680..., candidate 4f086575...), 1,300,276,404 -> 1,428,396,351 Ir here versus 1,300,394,281 -> 1,428,523,891 retained (both -0.009%: this run's minimal environment shortens glibc's __tunables_init scan and changes a little GC work), +9.853% in both. Attributed to #1004's byte scanner (pys_bytes_scan +87.8M) in bench/smoke/results/json-controls-2026-11-02.json; not re-investigated.

experiment_pys_list_set.what: Not a candidate measurement: the candidate compiler with PYSTACHY_HOME=$SCRATCH/perf/exp-home, a git-archive copy of c3aaa068 whose runtime.c drops only pys_list_set's identity-companion line (#888), and its own runtime cache. It shows how much of each change that one inlined branch carries. Binaries for barnes_hut, comprehensions, generators, spectral_norm, unpack_sequence, bench_fib and bench_nbody were byte-identical to the candidate's, so they were not re-counted; regex_v8 was not rebuilt.
experiment_pys_list_set.suite_effect: Over the 21 comparable pyperformance benchmarks other than regex_v8 (byte-identical binaries taken at the candidate's counts), the geomean change from alpha.3 is +2.379% for the candidate and +0.714% for this experiment. The line carries all of scimark's, nbody's and bench_spectral's regressions, 56% of float's and 31% of go's.

wall_time_pairs.method: Five pairs per benchmark, alpha.3 and candidate alternating (order flips every pair), each run pinned with taskset -c 3, same arguments and environment as the counts; ratio = candidate / alpha.3. Noisy shared-host timings (one-minute load about 2.3 from other agents during the pairs); raw samples, timed parts and load averages in $SCRATCH/perf/wall.json.
observations: Directions agree for bench_fib, scimark, raytrace, json_loads, barnes_hut and fannkuch, with smaller magnitudes than the instruction counts (bench_fib +6% wall versus +24% Ir, close to the recursion-guard report's 'about 5% slower').
generators: +13.3% Ir but about -1% wall (within noise).

regex_dna: +0.6% Ir but about 31% lower wall time. getrusage over three runs each: user time 0.167-0.171 s (alpha.3) versus 0.099-0.123 s (candidate), the same ~8,980 minor faults and ~19.4 MB peak RSS. A microarchitectural (layout/branch/memory) difference that callgrind does not model; not investigated.

caveats: Instruction counts are not wall time: callgrind counts each byte of a rep stosb memset as an instruction (allocation zeroing) and ignores cache misses, branch prediction and memory bandwidth.
Whole-process counts include startup, setup and untimed checks; regex_v8's (15.4 billion) is dominated by its untimed checksum pass, and unpack_sequence's (1.2 million) by startup.

Counts repeat to within a few tens of instructions for a fixed executable, arguments and environment (printed timings and clock reads vary); a different environment block changed json_loads by about 0.009% (glibc tunables scan and GC stack contents).
Shared host (4 vCPUs, three other agents): build times and the optional wall-time pairs are noisy, single machine indications.
The oracle is CPython 3.13.18 (python3.13 on this host), while the repository's .python-version pins 3.13.16, which earlier published results used; every output here matched 3.13.18 byte for byte.
Arguments differ from the controller's measured ones for 15 benchmarks (args_note), so these counts are not comparable with tools/bench_pyperformance.py timings.

microgpt is a reduced-size derivative of bench/microgpt/microgpt.py (10 steps, 3 samples), not the controller's instrumented run; its printed losses have 4 decimals, so last-digit float differences would not show.
Only AOT executables were measured; JIT (pystachy run) startup/compile cost and frontend compile time were not.
Paths are normalized: $CHECKOUT is the candidate checkout and $SCRATCH a private scratch directory (callgrind profiles, executables and the alpha.3 worktree are not retained in the repository).
